records.description: For the declared isothermal uniform bulk linear response, the proper piezoelectric stress tensor is e_ijk=(partial D_i/partial strain_jk) at fixed E,T, equivalently -(partial stress_jk/partial E_i) at fixed strain,T. Its SI units are C/m^2. The piezoelectric strain tensor d relates strain to electric field at fixed stress,T or displacement D to stress at fixed E,T, with units m/V, equivalently C/N. Converting between e and d requires elastic compliance and matching tensor/shear conventions; they are not interchangeable numerical coefficients.

The fixed-E and fixed-strain elastic/dielectric conventions, temperature, axis handedness and contracted shear factors are part of the definition. Intrinsic bulk coefficients and substrate-constrained effective thin-film coefficients are different quantities.

This formal linear-response definition is not a measured coefficient, ferroelectric domain history or universal statement about all surfaces, gradients, defects, frequencies and nonlinear electromechanical mechanisms. No new full point-group classification or electronic-structure dataset is admitted.

records.description: In the selected homogeneous hot-expanding model, weak neutron/proton interconversion, expansion and thermodynamics set a reaction history for free nucleons and light nuclei. Abundances may be expressed per baryon as Y_i=n_i/n_b; a nuclear species balance has dilution dn_i/dt+3*H*n_i and a sum of reaction production and destruction terms. These model equations require a supplied cosmological background, baryon density, weak rates, neutron lifetime and thermonuclear cross sections.
